title: Introduction to Digital Marketing
description: This is a competency-based course designed for the indentured Digital Marketer apprentice. This course provides an overview of digital marketing, including key channels such as search engines, social media, and email marketing. Apprentices will learn foundational concepts in branding, customer engag
learning_objectives: Describe the main digital marketing channels and how they map to stages of a customer journey
Write a positioning statement and on-brand messaging for a defined audience
Explain how search engines decide which pages to rank
Plan an organic social presence and respond to audience conversation appropriately
Design a basic email lifecycle sequence for a new subscriber
Select the right KPIs for a campaign goal and read a basic performance report

prerequisites: Basic computer literacy: web browsing, spreadsheets, and a word processor

lessons.title: Brand Foundations and Marketing Copy

lessons.title: How Search Marketing Works

lessons.title: Marketing Measurement Fundamentals

sequencing_rationale: This is the pathway's entry course, so it surveys every channel the later courses go deep on and teaches none of them to working depth. The order is landscape first (learners need the vocabulary and the funnel model before any single channel makes sense), then brand and copy (every channel is a delivery mechanism for a message, so the message comes first), then a one-lesson pass over each major channel in the order the pathway teaches them (search, social, email), then measurement (which only means something once the learner knows what is being measured), then privacy and ethics, and finally an integrating project. SCOPE ASSUMPTIONS - the intake description is truncated mid-word (it ends at 'customer engag') and supplied no objectives or lesson titles, so the following scope was inferred and needs reviewer confirmation: (1) 'customer engag[ement]' was read as engagement across the funnel - audience research, value proposition, and community response - and is taught conceptually in lessons 02, 03 and 05, not as CRM work (CRM is dm350). (2) 'branding' was scoped to positioning, voice, and messaging, not to visual identity, logo design, or brand asset production - no design competency exists in the catalog. (3) The named channels (search engines, social media, email) each get exactly one awareness-level lesson; the deep versions live in dm201, dm250 and dm350. (4) Privacy, ethics and ad policy were sited here because no other course in the pathway owns them end to end and every later course assumes them; if the reviewer would rather site them in dm350, lesson 08 moves. (5) Measurement here is KPI literacy only - tool work is dm301. Nothing in the truncated sentence was invented to complete it.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can map digital marketing channels to the stages of a customer journey and select a channel mix for a stated campaign goal.
proposed_competencies.rationale: Lesson 02 and the lesson 09 project both require cross-channel selection, but every catalog competency is scoped to a single channel; nothing covers choosing between them.
